title: Problem-focused vs emotion-focused coping
citation: Folkman, S., & Moskowitz, J. T. (2004). Coping: Pitfalls and promise. Annual Review of Psychology, 55, 745-774.
content:
Problem-focused vs Emotion-focused coping.

One of the most useful ways to understand coping is to distinguish between problem-focused coping and emotion-focused coping. Problem-focused coping aims to change or manage the source of stress, such as making a plan, asking for advice, or solving a practical issue. Emotion-focused coping aims to manage the emotional impact of a situation through approaches such as relaxation, mindfulness, self-compassion, or talking with someone you trust. Most people benefit from using both types, depending on what the situation requires.
